FAQ.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Is the initial consultation free?
items.answer: Yes, it is free of charge. We believe our role as consultants is to be a partner who works alongside you on your concerns and challenges. Our added value lies in the solutions we propose once we have explored your concerns in depth and identified the underlying issues. We help you identify those issues at no cost, so please feel free to contact us.

items.question: We are a small or medium-sized company. Can we still consult with you?
items.answer: Absolutely. Around 80% of our members have built their professional experience at major consulting firms known as the Big Four, yet our fees are roughly 50–70% of what those large firms charge. Thanks to our reputation for "Big Four quality at reasonable prices," about 80% of our clients are small and medium-sized businesses or individuals.

items.question: Which industries do you support?
items.answer: We support a wide range of industries, including manufacturing, finance, retail, IT, healthcare and education. Consultants familiar with industry-specific challenges will take charge of your project.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: Costs vary depending on the scope, duration and scale of the project. We will first listen to your needs and then propose the best plan along with a quotation. We are committed to transparent pricing.

items.question: Can you provide support remotely?
items.answer: Yes, we can support you online. We use video conferencing and chat tools to communicate efficiently, and we can also offer a hybrid of in-person and remote support as needed.

items.question: Is confidentiality guaranteed?
items.answer: Of course. We can also prepare a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) if needed, so you can rest assured.

CompanyInfo.heading: Company Overview
CompanyInfo.parentNote: (A professional services group centered on judicial scriveners, with 55 years of history in Tokyo)
history: 1969: Founder (now Chairman) Koki Kurosawa registers as a judicial scrivener
1972: Founds Kurosawa Joint Office, made up of judicial scriveners, in Nakano, Tokyo
2009: Incorporates the judicial scrivener division and opens the Yokohama office
2015: With business expansion, incorporates the land and house investigator division
2016: Opens the Inheritance Support Office specializing in inheritance and adult guardianship
2016: Founds KCV (Kurosawa Consulting Vietnam), the Vietnamese subsidiary
2025: Known for "high quality at reasonable prices," grows rapidly to more than 100 clients and more than 350 clients served

paragraphs: Kurosawa Consulting Vietnam provides comprehensive support for Japanese companies entering Vietnam. From market research to incorporation, licensing, recruitment and post-launch operational support, we offer a one-stop service.

Our team of specialists, well versed in Vietnam's regulations and business practices, proposes the entry structure best suited to your business plan and ensures a smooth setup. With our extensive local track record and attentive support in Japanese, even first-time entrants can rely on us with confidence.

faq.question: How long does it take to establish a company in Vietnam?
faq.answer: It depends on the industry and entry structure, but establishing a typical subsidiary takes about 3–6 months: roughly 2–3 months to obtain the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), followed by about 1–3 months for licenses and permits.

faq.question: What is the difference between a subsidiary and a representative office?
faq.answer: A subsidiary is an independent legal entity that can conduct sales activities and record revenue. A representative office, by contrast, is limited to market research and liaison activities and cannot conduct sales. We will propose the most suitable structure for your objectives.

faq.question: Can a company be 100% foreign-owned?
faq.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is possible in many industries. However, some industries (such as real estate and advertising) have foreign ownership restrictions and may require a joint venture with a Vietnamese company. Please check the requirements for your industry.

faq.question: What is the minimum capital requirement?
faq.answer: Vietnam generally has no minimum capital requirement, although some industries (such as banking and insurance) do. In practice, it is important to set capital appropriate to your business plan.

faq.question: Is support available in Japanese?
faq.answer: Yes. We have Japanese staff and Vietnamese staff fluent in Japanese, so you can work with us comfortably in Japanese.

faq.question: How long does an M&A of a Vietnamese company take?
faq.answer: It depends on the size and complexity of the deal, but generally takes about 6 months to 1 year. Due diligence and government approvals can take time.

faq.question: Are there restrictions on foreign acquisitions of Vietnamese companies?
faq.answer: Yes, foreign ownership restrictions apply depending on the industry. Some industries, such as banking, media and real estate, have limits on foreign ownership ratios. Please check each case individually.

faq.question: What does due diligence cover?
faq.answer: We investigate financial, tax, legal and business aspects, paying close attention to Vietnam-specific risks such as land use rights, labor law and tax risks.

faq.question: Can you also support PMI after the M&A?
faq.answer: Yes, we also provide PMI (post-merger integration) support, continuing through organizational integration, system integration and realizing synergies.

faq.question: Is support available in Japanese?
faq.answer: Yes. A bilingual team able to work with both your Japanese headquarters and the Vietnamese side will handle your project.

faq.question: Are Vietnamese accounting standards different from Japan's?
faq.answer: Yes. Vietnam uses Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS), which differ in some respects from Japanese GAAP and IFRS. Our staff are well versed in both.

faq.question: Can you prepare consolidation reports for our Japanese headquarters?
faq.answer: Yes, we prepare the reporting packages needed for your headquarters' consolidated accounts, including reclassification to Japanese GAAP.

faq.question: Can we request bookkeeping only?
faq.answer: Yes, we accept bookkeeping-only engagements. You can choose just the services you need.

faq.question: What is the corporate income tax rate in Vietnam?
faq.answer: The standard corporate income tax rate in Vietnam is 20%. Where tax incentives apply, reduced rates such as 10% or 15% may be available.

faq.question: Is support available in Japanese?
faq.answer: Yes. Staff fluent in Japanese will handle your account, and we can also prepare reports in Japanese.

faq.question: Is Vietnamese labor law very different from Japan's?
faq.answer: Yes, it differs in many respects, including types of labor contracts, probation periods, dismissal rules and social insurance. Our specialists provide advice based on Vietnamese labor law.

faq.question: Are contracts written in Japanese valid?
faq.answer: In Vietnam, it is recommended to prepare contracts in Vietnamese or attach a Vietnamese translation. In a dispute, the Vietnamese version may take precedence.

faq.question: Do you also support work permits for foreign employees?
faq.answer: Yes, we support work permit applications for foreign nationals. Please see our License Applications service for details.

faq.question: If a labor dispute arises, can you respond immediately?
faq.answer: Yes, we respond promptly to urgent labor issues. Please contact us by phone or email first.

faq.question: Do you offer retainer contracts?
faq.answer: Yes, we offer fixed monthly retainer contracts, recommended for companies that need ongoing legal and labor advice.

faq.question: How long does it take to obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC)?
faq.answer: Usually about 2–4 weeks, though it varies by industry and investment size. Conditional business lines require additional review and may take longer.

faq.question: Do required licenses differ by industry?
faq.answer: Yes, required licenses vary greatly by industry. Manufacturing, retail, food & beverage, IT and other sectors each require their own permits.

faq.question: What are the requirements for a foreign national's work permit?
faq.answer: Generally, a university degree or higher and at least three years of relevant work experience, or professional qualifications, are required. The position must also be one that cannot be filled by a Vietnamese national.

faq.question: Do you also support license renewals?
faq.answer: Yes, we support renewals and amendments, including managing renewal deadlines.

faq.question: Can we prepare documents in Japanese?
faq.answer: Applications to Vietnamese authorities must be prepared in Vietnamese. We handle translation and notarization for you.
